labels.label: prop:mesure_dieckmann_Lorentz
labels.notes: Unmarked, instance only, and correctly so. ETT.tex:1054-1061 was read in full: 'Let M be a strongly causal Lorentzian manifold. Then M admits a measure which is admissible both in the past and in the future.' minkowski_mesure_dieckmann (n : ℕ) : ∃ μ : Measure (Minkowski n), (minkowski n).AdmissiblePast μ ∧ (minkowski n).AdmissibleFuture μ has no hypothesis, no instance argument and no implicit beyond n. It is the paper's statement specialised to M = ℝ^{1,n}, for every n with n = 0 included, so Lean ≥ the specialisation. ONE measure serves both directions, as printed. The specialisation is legitimate: minkowski n is the standard cone causality (minkowski_le_top_iff: ‖q.2 − p.2‖ ≤ q.1 − p.1, and lt with <), on the product topology, and the paper's hypothesis holds on it (minkowski_stronglyCausal). Admissibility is the library's structure, printed in the probe. regular is mathlib's Measure.Regular on the Borel σ-algebra (the probe infers BorelSpace (Minkowski n)), which is condition 1. finite is condition 2. pos reads p < q as C.le ⊤ p q ∧ p ≠ q, the stronger reading against p ≪ q, which is condition 3. null quantifies over every A, read for the outer measure (rem:mesure_bord), with Kminus/Kplus transcribing defi:futur_continue (Reachable.lean:93-101), which is condition 4. The conclusion is not trivially inhabited, since pos excludes μ = 0. THE REDUCTION ADDS NO HYPOTHESIS. minkowski_mesure_dieckmann_of takes hreg, hfin, hpos and hnull, and minkowski_exists_measure discharges all four. minkowski_exists_measure is a term alias of Causal.Flat.minkowski_frontier_null_measure, whose type #check shows to be identical. That theorem fixes the MeasurableSpace of FlatSpacetime.minkowskiSpace n to the one of Minkowski n through letI, so it is the same σ-algebra. Conditions 3 and 4 are proved on this side, by staticCausality.exists_isOpen_subset_J∓_diff and by J^∓(A) ∖ K^∓(A) ⊂ ∂I^∓(A) with no extra hypothesis. Observation (not a defect): the statement is literally that of the strict Causal.Flat.minkowski_admissible_pair. The probe checks `@Causal.minkowski_mesure_dieckmann = @Causal.Flat.minkowski_admissible_pair := rfl`, which typechecks only if the two types agree. Graduation therefore adds a second proof of an existing strict theorem. What the module itself contributes is the Minkowski-specific reduction minkowski_mesure_dieckmann_of, through staticCausality rather than through GerochFlat's GH flat-spacetime route. The 4000-character window contains no ``**`label`**``; the ledger regex finds no mark in the file. The bold phrase in the docstring of minkowski_mesure_dieckmann_of does not match the regex. FINDING CHECKED, TRUE: the paper finding (ledger) that 'checks easily' rests on achronal boundaries being Lipschitz hypersurfaces (Hawking–Ellis Prop. 6.3.1) is right. In a strongly causal Lorentzian manifold J^∓(A) ⊂ cl I^∓(A) and K^∓ = I^∓, so condition 4 asks for the nullity of a subset of the achronal boundary ∂I^∓(A). Its wording 'The sorry'd existence statement' is stale (see finding 3).

findings.what: The docstring is stale since the cleanup and its wording needs to change at graduation. (a) l.11-13 says 'Kept in the scaffold until the ETT campaign graduates it; the instance-only scope below is why the row stays partial': the first clause becomes false on the move, and the second is false today (finding 3). (b) l.35-41, the SCOPE bullet 'The former `sorry`', says in the present tense 'what is missing is the nullity of ∂I^±(A)', and ends 'so the `sorry` is not vacuous', although nothing is missing and there is no sorry. (c) l.38-40 describes the route as 'I^-(A) = {t < f(x)}, f 1-Lipschitz … ∂I^-(A) lies in the graph of f, which is Lebesgue-null by Fubini; Causal/Flat/GerochFlat.lean proves it'. The library does not go through a Lipschitz graph. Causal/Flat/Geroch/ConeNull.lean ('Route (no Lipschitz graph needed)') shows that every vertical line meets the frontier of a locally past-closed set in at most one point, then applies Fubini–Tonelli. ChartNull and ChartMeasure carry this to a chart measure, and GerochFlat only assembles the result.
findings.fix: l.9-13: '`prop:mesure_dieckmann_Lorentz` — `ETT.tex:1054`, for Minkowski space only (the library has no Lorentzian manifolds). No `sorry`: the measure-theoretic input is `Causal.Flat.minkowski_frontier_null_measure` (DEC-65). The row is partial because the statement is an instance.' Replace the SCOPE bullet 'The former `sorry`' with: '**The measure** (`minkowski_exists_measure` = `Causal.Flat.minkowski_frontier_null_measure`; a tagged `sorry` until 2026-11-20): finite, regular, positive on non-empty open sets, and null on ∂I^±(A) for every `A`. The nullity is proved in `Causal/Flat/Geroch/ConeNull.lean` by vertical sections (each vertical line meets ∂I^∓(A) in at most one point; Fubini–Tonelli), carried to a chart measure by `Geroch/ChartNull`, `Geroch/ChartMeasure`.' Drop 'so the `sorry` is not vacuous'. Optionally mention that `Causal.Flat.minkowski_admissible_pair` has the identical statement.

The curation has lean_proved_override = "none", and the ledger prints Lean proved 'no', bucket C. Several curated fields are false since 18d8c16. blocked_on reads 'the null boundary of past sets … is not in mathlib'. notes ends '…, which is the tagged sorry. (WP-9, audited)', although campaign/WP-9 contains a REPORT and no AUDIT. paper_findings[1] says 'Row status for the ledger: stated', and paper_findings[0] says 'The sorry'd existence statement'. There is also a graduation trap. ledger.py:476-478 silently drops an extra_lean_file that no longer exists, so the scaffold path vanishes on the move. ledger.py:495-496 then computes 'closed' for any row whose files are strict with no counted sorry, because an unmarked file contributes 0. In paper_findings, replace 'The sorry'd existence statement' with 'The existence statement (proved)', and replace finding [1] with 'Row status: partial, Minkowski instance only (hypothesis strengthened).'
